messages.content: What's the population in New York right now?

function.name: time_converter
function.description: Converts the local time of user's region to the target region's local time. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

user_timezone.description: The timezone of the user in string format. Example: 'Pacific Time (US & Canada)'

target_timezone.description: The target timezone in string format where user wants to know the local time. Example: 'Eastern Time (US & Canada)'

time.description: The local time of user's timezone in string format (24 hr format). Optional parameter. Example: '15:30:00'

message.content:
I don’t have access to live demographic feeds, so I’m going off the most recent official estimates:

| Region | Latest Estimate |
|--------|----------------|
| **New York City** | ≈ 8.5 million residents (U.S. Census Bureau, 2022‑23 ACS) |
| **State of New York** | ≈ 19.9 million residents (Census Bureau, 2021‑22 ACS) |

These numbers come from the American Community Survey’s annual estimates and reflect changes since the 2020 decennial census. Population counts fluctuate slightly each year due to births, deaths, migration, etc., but there isn’t an instantaneous “real‑time” figure publicly released. If you need the absolute latest count—say, down to the minute—you’d typically look at specialized municipal databases or statistical agencies that publish daily snapshots, though those aren’t usually made public on demand.
message.reasoning:
The user asks about current population in New York. This requires up-to-date data; we don't have real-time info. We can provide approximate or mention latest census estimate and note it's not exact. No tool needed.

We should respond with best available knowledge as of last update. Provide context: NYC estimated ~8.5 million people per 2020 Census, slight growth. Also mention state population ~19.9M. Clarify no live updates.
